title: 2014 AMC 10B Problem 6
statement: Orvin went to the store with just enough money to buy \(30\) balloons. When he arrived, he discovered that the store had a special sale on balloons: buy \(1\) balloon at the regular price and get a second at \(\frac{1}{3}\) off the regular price. What is the greatest number of balloons Orvin could buy?

solutions.text:
Each pair of balloons costs \(1+\frac23=\frac53\) times the regular price of one balloon.

Thus, with the money for \(30\) regular-price balloons, Orvin can buy \(30\cdot\frac65=36\) balloons.

Thus, the correct answer is C .
hints: Pair each full-price balloon with its discounted companion
A two-balloon sale pair costs \(\frac53\) regular balloons
